title: 材料力学Ⅰ
subtitle: Strength of Materials I
teachers:
TANAKA Mototsugu
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: Investigating the strength of materials can clarify the forces that act on various parts of bridges, steel towers, cars, planes, energy equipment, living tissues and cells, etc., and the deformations they cause. The results can be used for safety design. It is therefore a foundational subject in mechanical engineering. In this course, students will gain a thorough understanding of the investigation of the strength of materials through lectures and practice.
advice:
This is a basic strength of materials course. We will cover the following topics:

1. Stress and strain                                     5. Beams and their support conditions
2. Hooke’s law                                           6. Shearing forces and bending moments of beams
3. Mechanical properties of materials        7. Bending stress in a beam
4. Allowable stress and safety factors        8. Deflection of a beam

In this course, it is important to do many practice exercises, but the study of the strength of materials is extremely difficult to understand just by memorizing formulas and patterns. To solve a problem, one should start with an understanding of the basic formulas needed, and then set the appropriate boundary conditions for the problem. In addition, it is necessary to be able to concretely imagine the actual forces, moments, and deformations using schematic diagrams.
Furthermore, students should work on issues related to local companies, and deepen their understanding of the relationship between the strength of materials and society/technology.
books:
Textbooks: Basis of Understanding Strength of Materials, 2nd edition, Kyoritsu Shuppan Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reference books: Basic Strength of Materials, Morikita Publishing Co. Ltd. (in Japanese)
Reserved books: Unspecified
requiredKnowledge: Gaining understanding by working through many different problems is the best way to learn strength of materials. As a prerequisite, it is necessary to fully understand "Industrial Mechanics I". In addition, students will be expected to move on to "Strength of Materials II" and "Strength of Materials III", which will be offered subsequently, as they are applications of this course.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the concept of normal stress, shear stress, normal strain, shear strain, and Hooke's law.
Be able to explain the deformation and fracture behavior of materials by drawing stress-strain characteristics.
Be able to explain the relationship between material properties, reference strength, and the allowable stress.
Be able to explain the shearing force and bending moment generated in a beam by drawing SFDs and BMDs.
Be able to determine the stress and deflection that occur in a beam and to perform safety design.
Be able to explain the relationship between strength of materials and society/technology.

achievementLevels.ideal:
1. Understand the concept of stress and strain.
2. Distinguish the nominal stress and true stress, nominal strain and true strain.
3. Design safe structures using standard strength and allowable stress.
4. Draw SFDs and BMDs for various beams loaded with a concentrated load and an equally distributed load.
5. Calculate bending stress and deflection of various beams and indeterminant beam and achieve a safe design.
6. Understand in depth the relationship between the strength of materials and society/technology.
achievementLevels.standard:
1. Calculate stresses and strains.
2. Perform calculations on the basis of safety factors.
3. Draw SFDs and BMDs of a cantilever beam and a simple support beam loaded with a concentrated load and an equally distributed load.
4. Calculate the bending stress and deflection of  a cantilever beam and a simple support beam loaded with a concentrated load and an equally distributed load.
5. Understand the relationship between strength of materials and society/technology.
